google-flow.role: Google tool for creating AI video clips, scenes and stories.
google-flow.audience: Creators aged 18+; Google presents Flow as built with and for creators.
google-flow.status: Active. Google announced Veo 3.1 Fast, Veo 3.1 Quality and Omni Flash 1.1 will be retired on 5 Dec 2026 (not yet at check time); Veo 3.1 Lite is not included. Veo Extend was already retired on 5 Nov 2026. Pages don't say what happens to existing projects.
pros: Daily free quota, even without a subscription: non-subscribers get 50 Flow credits a day.
Several creation modes in one tool: with Omni Flash 1.2 you can create video from text, from frames (web only) and from reference material, and edit existing video.
Longer clips, extension and upscaling for subscribers: paid plans create 3 to 15 second clips, extend them by 3 to 10 seconds and upscale Omni videos from 360p to 1080p. 4K upscaling is Ultra only.
cons: Models retire on short notice: three video models are planned to retire on 5 Dec 2026; Veo Extend already retired 5 Nov 2026.

Free use is short and may be blocked at peak hours: without a subscription, video generation may be unavailable at peak hours (about 14:00 to 17:00 UTC). Clips are 3 to 10 seconds and unused daily credits don't accumulate.

Veo models are short and limited: Veo 3.1 Lite makes 4, 6 or 8 second clips at 720p, with no editing of existing video and no extension. Veo 3.1 Quality has no reference-based generation, editing or extension.
google-flow.price: Google AI Pro: 19.99 USD/month billed monthly. Price of the cheaper Google AI Plus not verified. Free daily quota.
google-flow.model: Credits that come with a Google AI subscription; Flow isn't sold separately.
google-flow.free: 50 Flow credits a day without a subscription, not accumulating. 3 to 10 second clips with Omni Flash 1.2. Video generation may be unavailable at peak hours.
google-flow.trial: The plans page mentions a trial for Google AI subscribers; length and terms not verified.
plans: 200 Flow credits/month, 3,000 Flow Music credits, 400GB storage.
1,000 Flow credits/month, 10,000 Flow Music credits, 5TB storage.
1,000 Flow credits/month, 10,000 Flow Music credits, 5TB storage.
10,000 Flow credits/month, 20TB storage. Price 100 USD per the Flow help page, 99.99 in the plans-page calculator.
25,000 Flow credits/month, 30TB storage. About 200 USD per the Flow help page.
google-flow.privacy: Partially verified only. The official FAQ lists training new models among uses of user data, but the full sentence and context weren't read. Flow's intro page doesn't address training. Flow's own privacy policy not checked.
google-flow.rights: Google says it doesn't claim ownership of original content created in its services, and use is subject to the terms of service. Explicit commercial-use permission per plan wasn't verified.
google-flow.watermark: All Veo, Omni and Nano Banana outputs carry an invisible SynthID watermark. A visible watermark is controlled by a toggle in the profile menu and applied automatically to users in India, South Korea and Vietnam who aren't Google AI Ultra 20x subscribers.
google-flow.api: Yes, via Google. No API for Flow itself found, but Google's video models are open to developers through the Gemini API (Gemini Omni Flash about 0.10 USD per video second at 720p, no free tier).
google-flow.hebrew: The official availability page lists Hebrew among Flow's supported languages and Israel among supported countries, and recommends writing prompts in English for best results. It doesn't detail what support includes (Hebrew interface, RTL display, Hebrew speech, lip sync not verified).
google-flow.students: Per the plans page, students get Google AI Pro free for a year, or Google AI Pro with YouTube Premium at 8.99 USD/month. Benefits last up to four years, need SheerID verification and aren't available on school accounts.
google-flow.watch: After an August 2026 update Android users reported generation errors and downloads at 720p instead of 1080p.

runway.role: Platform for creating video and images with many models, plus music, voice and effects.
runway.audience: Independent creators, from a first try at AI video to heavy use, plus teams and organizations.
runway.status: Active. The Unlimited plan is being replaced by Max: Max has been offered to new subscribers since 29 May 2026, and existing Unlimited subscribers are due to move on 30 Nov 2026 (not yet done at check time).
pros: Many models in one subscription: per the pricing page, Standard and up include all video and image models, including Gen-4.5, Aleph 2.0, Kling 4.0, Seedance 2.0 Pro, Gen-4 Image and Nano Banana Pro.
Documented API with a public price list: an API credit costs 0.01 USD and each model has a published credits-per-second rate.
Production extras on higher plans: Pro adds unlimited 4K video upscaling, one brand kit, one voice clone and Runway MCP. Max adds HDR output, ProRes and image sequences.
cons: Free plan is a one-time grant with a watermark: 125 one-time credits that don't renew, no option to buy more. Every free video carries a Runway watermark.
Credit quota covers short video on advanced models: Standard's 625 credits equal about 52 seconds of Gen-4.5 (60 credits per 5 seconds). Aleph 2.0 costs 140 credits per 5 seconds.
Unused credits are deleted on the cheaper plans: on Standard and Pro monthly credits don't roll over. Only Max, and per the help page Team, keeps them for up to a month.
runway.price: From 15 USD/month billed monthly, or 12 USD/month billed annually. Free plan with 125 one-time credits.
runway.free: Permanent free plan: 125 one-time credits that don't expire or renew, a limited changing model selection and 5GB storage. Videos carry a watermark.
plans: 125 one-time credits, limited changing model selection, 5GB storage.
625 credits/month, all video and image models, no watermark, 4K upscaling, 5 concurrent generations, up to 3 projects, 20GB storage.
Same as monthly Standard.
2,250 credits/month, 15 concurrent generations, up to 5 projects, one brand kit, one voice clone, buy extra credits, Runway MCP, unlimited 4K video upscaling.
Same as monthly Pro.
9,500 credits/month, early access to new models, 20 concurrent generations, up to 10 projects, up to 3 brand kits and voice clones, HDR, ProRes and image sequence output.
Same as monthly Max.
runway.privacy: Not verified. The official terms (last updated 23 Oct 2026) loaded, but no model-training clause was found and full text wasn't read. Privacy policy not checked. A paid subscription alone doesn't guarantee content isn't used for training.
runway.rights: Per a Runway help article, content you create belongs to you, Runway puts no non-commercial restrictions on it and you don't have to credit Runway. The article doesn't distinguish plans.
runway.watermark: Every video made on Free carries a Runway watermark. Standard and up have none.
runway.api: Yes. Documented API with a developer portal. A credit costs 0.01 USD, bought per project. Example rates in credits per video second: Gen-4.5 is 12, Gen-4 Turbo 5, Aleph 2.0 28.
runway.students: An official help article on student and educator discounts exists but its content didn't load: discount size, eligible plans and verification weren't verified. The pricing page shows no student price.
runway.watch: Users report credits are deducted even for failed generations, and that refunds are hard to get.

kling.role: Video and image generator from text and images, with built-in audio.
kling.audience: Independent creators, teams and organizations, per a plan ladder that includes Team and Enterprise.
kling.status: Active. Old klingai.com addresses redirect to kling.ai (seen 18.11.2026); no official announcement or date for the move. The homepage shows Kling 4.0 as the current model.
pros: Subscribers may use outputs commercially: per the paid terms of service, subscribers' commercial use of outputs is unrestricted except for building competing products, and subscribers may remove the brand watermark.
Up to 30-second video in Kling 4.0: the homepage shows up to 30-second generation, up to 10 key frames and up to 15 reference assets in Omni Reference.

Built-in speech in several languages: the Kling 3.0 launch announcement lists English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean and Spanish, including dialogue between characters speaking different languages (Feb 2026, previous model generation).
cons: Content may be used for model training by default: clause 4.7.3(f) lets Kling use input and outputs to train and develop models. You can withdraw permission for future use by emailing support@kling.ai.
No commercial use without a subscription: non-subscribers may not use outputs commercially and must label them with the Kling brand unless they get written approval.
No refunds, and subscription credits expire: payment isn't refunded after the service is activated. Subscription credits are valid one month from distribution; separately purchased credits two years.
kling.model: Monthly or annual subscription with credits, auto-renewing. Credit packs also sold: on the US App Store from 100 credits at 1.49 USD up to 3,300 credits at 50 USD.
kling.free: New users get free credits at sign-up, and returning users can get another grant on login each month. Amounts and validity may change; exact amount not verified.
kling.trial: No free trial of a paid plan found. The iOS app sells a one-week Standard subscription at 1.19 or 1.49 USD.
kling.privacy: The user grants Kling a non-exclusive royalty-free license on input and outputs, including for promotion, product development and sublicensing to third parties. The terms don't distinguish plans, and no source shows a paid subscription prevents training use. No official statement on handling data in Team and Enterprise. Per the privacy policy data is stored on servers in Singapore.
kling.rights: Content belongs to the user and Kling doesn't claim ownership. Subscribers may use outputs commercially without limit except building or offering competing products. Non-subscribers need approval.
kling.watermark: Non-subscribers must label outputs with Kling's brand and logo, or state clearly they were made with Kling AI. Subscribers may remove the watermark. The official FAQ says watermarks vary by plan, without a per-plan table.
kling.api: Yes. An official developer platform, KlingAI Open Platform, with a pricing page and docs. Pages weren't read, so API prices and model list weren't verified.
kling.hebrew: Not mentioned in source. Declared iOS interface languages: English, Japanese, Korean, Simplified and Traditional Chinese. Kling 3.0 speech languages: English, Chinese, Japanese, Korean, Spanish.
kling.watch: Users report credits are deducted even for failed or unusable results, and that there are no refunds.

hailuo.role: Video and image generator from text, images and reference material, with synchronized audio.
hailuo.audience: Independent creators and small teams in the app, and developers and businesses via the MiniMax API and open weights.
hailuo.status: Active. The current model, MiniMax H3, is available on the site and in the app; its launch date wasn't verified from an official source (an academic source, NYU Shanghai, gives 30 July 2026). The Unlimited plan is an old plan sold only until June 2025.
pros: Video and audio created together: MiniMax H3 produces video with synchronized stereo sound in one run, in clips up to 15 seconds and up to 2K via the API.
Broad control through reference material: the Ref2VA version accepts up to 9 images, 3 video clips and 3 audio clips as references. FL2VA lets you set the first frame, last frame or both.
Open model weights: H3 weights are free under the MiniMax H3 Community License, royalty-free, for research and commercial use, on Hugging Face, ModelScope and GitHub.
cons: Free has a watermark and credits expire fast: free downloads carry a watermark. New-user bonus credits expire after three days, subscription credits don't roll over, and paid payments aren't refunded.
Broad irrevocable license on your content: per the terms of use, the user grants the company a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license on uploaded content and outputs.
Open weights are restricted: not available in the EU, UK, US and South Korea. Companies with annual revenue over 20M USD need separate written approval.
hailuo.price: From 9.99 USD/month per the official blog of July 2026. Billing type not stated. Free plan exists.
hailuo.free: A free plan exists. Per subscription terms (14.7.2025, old source): downloads carry a watermark and up to three tasks can be queued. Current free credit amount not verified.
hailuo.trial: No free trial of a paid plan found. New-user bonus credits expire three days after being granted (old source).
hailuo.privacy: The user grants the company a worldwide, perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free license on uploaded content and outputs. The privacy policy (Dec 2025, old source) says personal data generally isn't transferred outside Singapore and face images and derived face data are deleted permanently after video generation. No difference between plans was found.
hailuo.rights: Per subscription terms (14.7.2025, old source), the company doesn't claim ownership of content created and downloaded under a paid subscription, and the subscription includes commercial-use rights.
hailuo.watermark: Free-plan downloads carry a watermark. Per subscription terms (old source), Standard and up download without one. The terms forbid removing, hiding or changing a watermark, metadata or label without written approval.
hailuo.api: Yes. The API is offered at platform.minimax.io in monthly video packages: Standard at 1,000 USD for 3,760 video credits, Pro at 2,500 USD for 9,920, Scale at 4,500 USD for 18,900, Business at 6,000 USD.

luma.role: Browser creation environment for producing video, images and audio with Ray models.
luma.audience: Per Luma, the model was developed with creators in entertainment, advertising and games; Team and Enterprise plans target creative teams.
luma.status: Renamed: a move from product to product, not just a rename. Dream Machine has a separate billing system and credits don't transfer between it and Luma Agents. No date given for closing sign-ups or fully shutting down Dream Machine. The official help article announcing it was updated on 22 May, year not stated.
pros: Precise control with keyframes: Ray3.2 supports up to 16 keyframes in a clip for control of pacing, motion and camera path.
HDR output for post-production: Ray3.2 produces native 1080p HDR with 16-bit EXR export. A third-party review of Ray3 also notes this.

Change the shot after generation: Enhanced Reframe changes aspect ratio, expands the frame or swaps the background while keeping the original lighting. Performance tracking captures pose, gestures and facial expressions of up to eight faces.
cons: Short clips: the official max length in Ray3.2 is 20 seconds per clip. A third-party review of Ray3 says longer content needs stitching in an outside tool.

Credits expire and high settings are expensive: unused credits expire at the end of the billing cycle. Per the API price table, a 10-second 1080p clip costs 1,200 credits, HDR doubles the price and HDR with EXR triples it.
Fine details don't always come out: per a third-party review, hands and fingers are inconsistent, text inside video is unreliable, and some human actions and spatial accuracy are hard.
luma.price: From 30 USD/month billed monthly, or 25 USD/month billed annually. No free plan on the pricing page.
luma.free: Not verified. No free plan on the official pricing page. The homepage and app page have a free-trial button with no detail on amount or limits.
luma.trial: Not verified. Luma's info page says free trial credits are included in all plans, without saying how many. Per the help article, a credit card is required at every sign-up, even for a free account.
plans: 10,000 credits, Luma and third-party image and video models, commercial use, edit permission for guest collaborators.
Same as monthly Plus.
40,000 credits, 4x Luma Agents usage, everything in Plus.
Same as monthly Pro.
150,000 credits, 15x Luma Agents usage, everything in Pro.
Same as monthly Ultra.
luma.privacy: Per the terms of use, the user grants Luma a worldwide, non-exclusive, irrevocable license on content. No option to refuse training is described, and deleting an account doesn't cancel licenses on content already incorporated. The privacy policy doesn't distinguish plans. For the API there is a commitment not to train on content: on the API page it appears on the Scale plan; per developer docs it applies to all plans.
luma.rights: Per the terms of use, the customer owns the outputs. Commercial use is allowed only for outputs created during an active subscription; for outputs created outside a subscription Luma gets a broader license.
luma.watermark: Not verified per plan. The pricing page mentions no watermark on any plan. Per the terms, Luma may embed watermarks, content credentials and provenance metadata in outputs, and they may not be removed or bypassed.
luma.api: Yes. Luma's API offers Ray3.2 (text to video, image to video, video to video and Reframe, at 1080p, HDR and 16-bit EXR) and the image model Uni-1.1, with Python and JavaScript/TypeScript SDKs.
luma.hebrew: Not mentioned in source. The app page says videos can be adapted to several languages with lip sync, without saying which. On 2 Sep 2026 Luma announced Arabic will be the first interface language besides English, launching later this year.
luma.students: No student discount found. There is an education program with an application form for educators and an interest form for student ambassadors, but the page states no discount, free credits or price.

pika.role: Platform for creating and editing short videos, images and audio.
pika.audience: Short social-media content creators per a third-party review; developers and agent builders are served through Pika API Club and Pika MCP.
pika.status: Active. The free plan now includes 0 monthly credits, per the official pricing page. Only a third-party tracking site gives the date of the change: it first saw the drop from 80 credits to 0 on 20 Sep 2026 (an observation date, not an official announcement). Basic, Standard, Pro and Unlimited are old plan names, and the old site old.pika.art still exists.
pros: Many models in one account: one account gives access to Pika's own models, Pika 2.5 and Pika H3 Flex, and to other companies' video, image and audio models. Per the pricing page all models are available on every plan.
No watermark on any plan: the pricing page states download without a watermark on all plans, including Free.

Easy and fast for short creative clips: per a third-party review from Aug 2026, among the easiest tools in the field, with fast rendering, an effects kit and image-to-video. Written before the current price list.
cons: You can't create on the free plan without paying: Free has 0 monthly credits and no commercial license. To create you must buy a credit pack or a subscription.
Weak consistency between shots: per a third-party review, faces, clothes and object shapes may change shot to shot, motion may distort fine details, and logos and labels need frame-by-frame checking.
No Android app: per the download page Pika publishes no Android version, so an app named Pika on Google Play isn't theirs.
pika.price: From 10 USD/month billed monthly, or 8 USD/month billed annually. The free plan has no monthly credits.
pika.model: Subscription with credits, alongside one-time credit packs
pika.free: Permanent Free plan at 0 USD but with 0 monthly credits: to create you must buy a credit pack or a subscription. Gives access to all models and downloads without a watermark.
pika.trial: The pricing page describes no time-limited trial.
plans: 0 monthly credits (credit packs only), all models, 2 concurrent videos, 2 concurrent image or audio generations, no watermark, no commercial license.
600 credits/month, 2 concurrent videos, 8 concurrent image or audio generations, no watermark, commercial license.
Same as monthly Starter.
2,600 credits/month, 8 concurrent videos, 32 concurrent image or audio generations, no watermark, commercial license.
Same as monthly Creator.
8,550+ credits/month, unlimited concurrent generation, priority queue, commercial license.
Same as monthly Fancy.
pika.privacy: None of the documents describes a general setting to opt out of training, and there is no distinction between Free, Starter, Creator and Fancy. On account deletion Pika commits to reasonable effort to remove content from future training, but content already incorporated into trained models may remain. Personal data sent via the API will generally be used to improve and train models.
pika.rights: Per the terms, Pika doesn't claim ownership of input or outputs, and rights in outputs stay with the user; however the terms note outputs may not receive copyright protection.
pika.watermark: No watermark on any plan, including Free, per the pricing page. The terms of use don't mention watermarks.
pika.api: Yes. Pika API Club: 10 USD/month membership that returns about 10 USD of API credits monthly, and beyond that pay-per-use at member rates. One key gives access to 100+ video, image and audio models.
pika.hebrew: Not mentioned in source. The homepage shows multilingual voice models without saying which languages are available in Pika.

higgsfield.role: Platform for creating video and images that gathers other companies' models alongside its own tools.
higgsfield.audience: Content creators and teams producing ads, social content and client work.
higgsfield.status: Active. New terms of use and privacy policy took effect in summer 2026. No announcement of closure, acquisition or rename. Per the independent sources read, the company's own models are mainly for images and it has no leading video model of its own. One review (SaaS CRM Review) says Cinema Studio 4.0 runs on Seedance 2.5; not verified.
pros: Many models in one account: alongside Higgsfield's own models (Soul, Popcorn, Higgsfield DOP), other companies' video models are available in the same place, including Veo, Seedance, Kling, Wan, Grok Imagine and more.
Its own cinematic-camera layer: Higgsfield DOP is described as the company's own layer, with visual effects and ready camera moves for image-to-video.
Wide access for developers and agents: pay-per-use API with Python and TypeScript SDKs, and MCP and CLI connections for agents such as Claude or Cursor.
cons: Your content may be used to train models: per the official terms summary, content helps improve the models and there is no general opt-out. The only stated ways to stop it are deleting the account or an enterprise agreement, and content already in models isn't removed.
Free plan has no monthly credits: it has no monthly or daily credit allotment, and its outputs may carry a visible watermark that stays on those files after upgrading.
Limits on credit packs: pack credits expire 90 days after purchase. Packs and auto-refill need an active subscription, and auto-refill isn't available on Starter.
higgsfield.price: From 19 USD/month billed monthly. Free plan without monthly credits.
higgsfield.free: Free plan without monthly or daily credits, one generation at a time and a limited model selection.
higgsfield.trial: Trial offers are personalized and not available on every account. A one-time paid access of 3 USD is also offered: 40 credits and two days of unlimited use.
plans: Limited model selection, no monthly credits, one generation at a time.
270 credits/month, 2 concurrent videos.
270 credits/month. Regular annual price not verified.
1,200 credits/month, 6 concurrent videos.
1,200 credits/month. Regular annual price not verified.
3,000 credits/month (6,000 or 9,000 also selectable), 8 concurrent videos.
3,000 credits/month. Regular annual price not verified.
2,500 credits per user in a shared pool, for 5 to 15 team members, basic unified sign-in.
higgsfield.privacy: Per Higgsfield, deleting content or the account stops future training use, but content already in trained models isn't removed. Deleted content can be restored for 30 days. Only for Enterprise does it say customer input and output aren't used for training; nothing like that is said about any paid personal plan. Full text of the current terms wasn't read; based on summaries.
higgsfield.rights: Per Higgsfield, outputs are owned by the user and rights stay with them after cancelling. For the free plan there is a contradiction between two official sources.
higgsfield.watermark: Download without a watermark is included in paid plans. Free-plan outputs may carry a visible watermark, embedded at generation, that stays on those files after upgrading.
higgsfield.api: Yes. The API is a separate product from the website subscription: pay-per-use from a prepaid balance in dollars, minimum top-up 5 USD. Video is billed per second and images per image, and only successfully completed generations are charged.

vidu.role: Video generator from text, image and reference material, built on its own models.
vidu.audience: Independent creators, small studios and production teams.
vidu.status: Active. Vidu Q4 Preview, a public preview of the next flagship model, was announced 7 Oct 2026 (per a press release not re-read) with launch prices. No announcement of closure, acquisition or rename.
pros: High resolution in the new model: Vidu Q4 Preview produces 2K or 4K video at 10-bit color depth, and also 540p, 720p and 1080p.
Broad control with reference material: Vidu Q4 Preview accepts up to 15 reference images and up to 3 audio clips.
Relatively long clips and API access: per the API docs, clip length is 1 to 16 seconds in viduq3-pro and 3 to 16 seconds in viduq4-preview.
cons: No refunds: the official pricing page says no refunds are given, and cancelling a subscription is done by emailing support.
Subscription credits expire fast: credits included in a subscription are valid only 30 days. Separately purchased and bonus credits are valid two years.

Limited free output: per an official May 2026 blog, the free plan is limited to 720p, every video carries a visible watermark in the bottom-right corner, and videos aren't allowed for commercial use. The source is about six months old.
vidu.free: Free plan at 0 USD: use the Q4 model at 540p at 2 credits per second and 10 reference materials a month. New users get trial credits at sign-up.
plans: Q4 at 540p at 2 credits per second, 10 reference materials/month, bonus credits on login.
800 credits/month, 3 to 16 second videos, up to 4 videos at once, commercial use of outputs. 8.25 USD/month on annual billing.
800 credits/month. Monthly price not verified (inferred about 10 USD).
3,500 credits/month, quota of 20 videos a day at off-peak hours, commercial use of outputs. 35.42 USD/month on annual billing.
3,500 credits/month. Monthly price not verified (inferred about 43 USD).
Quota of 200 videos a day at off-peak hours, commercial use of outputs. 95.83 USD/month on annual billing.
Monthly price not verified (inferred about 115 USD).
vidu.privacy: Not verified. The API platform's privacy policy loaded only as a table of contents with sections on data retention and deletion; nothing about model training was read. The consumer site's terms of use and privacy policy weren't located.
vidu.rights: The Standard, Premium and Ultimate plan cards on the official pricing page say outputs may be used commercially. Per an official May 2026 blog, free-plan videos aren't allowed for commercial use.
vidu.watermark: Per an official May 2026 blog, free-plan videos carry a visible watermark in the bottom-right corner, and removing it is tied to paid plans. Exactly which plans download without a watermark wasn't verified.
vidu.api: Yes. Official API platform at platform.vidu.com with Vidu models only (Q4 Preview, Q3, Q2, Q1 and Vidu 2.0) and extras such as digital avatar, audio and image generation. Billing in credits.

dreamina.role: Video creation from text, images and reference files using Seedance models.
dreamina.audience: Per the official pricing page: professional workflows and advertising uses.
dreamina.status: Active. The plan lineup was replaced: the pricing page shows Pro, Max and the earlier Standard as historical prices; current plans are Basic, Standard, Advanced and Ultra. There is an official page on Seedance 2.5 (from 24 Oct 2026), but its launch date and inclusion in plans weren't verified. The card's strengths describe Seedance 2.0.
pros: Several shots in one video: per a third-party review (Curious Refuge), generating several shots in one video is one of Seedance 2.0's main capabilities.
Audio and lip sync together with the video: per the same review, audio and lip sync are generated together with the video.
Up to 12 input files of different types: per an older third-party review (eWeek, Feb 2026), the model takes up to 12 files: images for style, video for motion and audio for rhythm.
cons: Anti-commercial clause in the US terms: in the US terms of use the user agrees not to use the service or its content for commercial purposes, while elsewhere commercial use is mentioned 'if permitted' without saying when. The contradiction isn't resolved in the text.
Data may be used to train models: the US privacy policy allows using data to train and improve models, and no option to refuse is described.
Visible flaws and distortions: per a third-party review (Curious Refuge), outputs show flaws and distorted details, and background edges look over-polished and plastic.
dreamina.price: From 15 USD/month billed monthly, per the US price list. Free daily credits.
dreamina.model: Subscription with credits. At 720p a second costs 17 credits in Seedance 2.0 Pro, 8 in Fast and 5 in Mini.
dreamina.free: Free daily credits to try Seedance 2.0. Amount not stated; per the page, credit amounts, watermarks and model access may change.
dreamina.trial: The source describes no trial period. First-month prices are an introductory discount on paid plans, not a free trial. Per the US terms, the subscription renews automatically.
plans: 1,575 credits/month (19 ten-second videos per the page); download without the Dreamina watermark.
3,885 credits/month (48 ten-second videos per the page); download without the Dreamina watermark.
17,600 credits/month (220 ten-second videos per the page); download without the Dreamina watermark.
59,000 credits/month (737 ten-second videos per the page); download without the Dreamina watermark.
dreamina.privacy: Only the US privacy policy (updated 30 Apr 2026) was read, and it applies to US users. Per it, user content is scanned, analyzed and reviewed, and information is shared with TikTok USDS affiliates. Storage location isn't stated. The policy that applies to users in Israel wasn't read.
dreamina.rights: Unclear from the official terms; only the US terms of use were read. Per them the user owns the input and outputs as long as they comply with the terms, and the company receives a worldwide license.
dreamina.watermark: On all four paid plans: download without the Dreamina watermark. On free use, per the page, watermarks may change.
dreamina.hebrew: Not mentioned in source. The site has versions in other languages (including German, French and Korean), and no Hebrew version was seen; that is no evidence either way.

wan.role: Creation platform producing video and images from text and images, including editing.
wan.audience: Inference: creators working on wan.video and developers using the model through Alibaba Cloud Model Studio; official sources don't define a target audience.
wan.status: Active. The official homepage promotes Wan3.0. Its launch date wasn't verified from an official source (a news source, The Next Web, gives 24 Aug 2026). The API docs read (updated 11 Oct 2026) still describe wan2.7, with no deprecation notice. The consumer product is called Wan Create. Per one third-party source (howaiworks.ai), only Wan 2.2 from July 2025 is open for download and local running; versions 2.5 to 3.0 are closed and cloud-only. The card's strengths and limits rest on a Wan 2.7 review.
pros: 30-second video and up to 20 reference files: the official homepage shows Wan3.0 with 30 seconds in sequence, up to 20 reference files and video editing.

Fine details, camera movement and built-in audio: per a third-party review (Curious Refuge) of Wan 2.7: details like skin texture and atmospheric lighting, cinematic camera movement and background audio generated with the video.
Developer access billed per second: model wan2.7-t2v is available via Alibaba Cloud Model Studio with per-second pricing, including a 1080P tier and a limit of 300 requests a minute per region.
cons: Physics errors and illogical motion: per a third-party review (Curious Refuge) of Wan 2.7, videos show physics errors and illogical motion.
First period of a subscription isn't refundable: per the pricing page, the subscription auto-renews and can be cancelled any time, but the first month or first year isn't refundable after activation.
The API doesn't support fine-tuning: the wan2.7-t2v model page says fine-tuning, batch processing and context caching aren't supported.
wan.price: From 10 USD/month billed monthly, or 5 USD/month billed annually. Free plan exists.
wan.free: Free plan: one video and one image at a time, 6 image styles and free credits on daily login. Credit amount not stated.
plans: One video and one image at a time, 6 image styles, free credits on daily login.
300 credits/month (up to 1,200 images or 60 videos), 3 concurrent videos, no-watermark download, 1080p video, 10 to 30 second videos.
Same as monthly Pro.
1,200 credits/month (up to 4,800 images or 240 videos), 8 concurrent videos, no-watermark download, 1080p video, 10 to 30 second videos.
Same as monthly Premium.
wan.privacy: Not verified. The site links to a privacy policy, terms of use, a usage policy and a Training Data Summary document, but they weren't read.
wan.rights: Not verified. Terms of use weren't read, and no official statement on commercial rights in outputs was found.
wan.watermark: On Pro and Premium: download of images and videos without a watermark. For the free plan the source doesn't say.
wan.api: Yes. Through Alibaba Cloud Model Studio, in China (Beijing), Singapore (international) and Japan (Tokyo) regions. The price is separate from the consumer subscription and is set per second.
wan.hebrew: Not mentioned in source. The API model page also doesn't say which languages prompts can be written in.
